fieldsRead.text: Radboud’s English-taught Artificial Intelligence bachelor studies human cognition and develops intelligent computer systems. Programming, mathematics, statistics, robotics, neuroscience, language and philosophy support a 180 EC degree with restricted electives, free choice and a required thesis.

Three related UCR programmes emphasise broad AI and cognition, computational intelligent systems, or cognitive neuroscience and language. Each contains substantial AI methods but differs from Radboud’s integrated specialist sequence. Human language study is distinct from computational NLP, and the UCR schedules do not replace the separate Radboud thesis.

This new-entrant pathway uses the current 2026–2027 regulations. Prospective webpages describe an indicative overview that may change; future cohort availability is not guaranteed. Year 2 contains 12 EC restricted choices and year 3 contains 24 EC restricted choices plus 24 EC free electives. Cognitive Science is restricted to second-year AI students from cohort 2025, so it is not selected for this pathway. Year 2 requires positive study advice; year 3 requires all first-year units; the thesis requires 120 EC. RADAr English is an additional 0 EC requirement. The programme publishes a 42 EC first-year continuation threshold, subject to personal circumstances.

UCR offers search, optimisation and probabilistic-agent methods. The available evidence does not establish a selected counterpart for the Knowledge Based AI component’s primary knowledge-representation and reasoning focus.

UCR numerical methods develops approximation, quadrature and numerical differential equations. This has a different primary method from the comparator’s second calculus unit; no calculus-course equivalence is asserted.

Radboud integrates computing, mathematics, statistics, cognitive science, neuroscience, linguistics and philosophy with a required 12-EC thesis. UCR offers substantial AI study with different computational and cognitive emphases. Bayesian-network methods occur in its intelligent-agent course; dedicated Bayesian statistics, symbolic knowledge representation, NLP, human-centred design, brain-computer interfacing and theoretical cognitive modelling are less fully represented. Signal processing occurs in the broad option. Human psycholinguistics and deep-learning language applications do not reproduce a dedicated NLP sequence. Scheduled research and evidence synthesis do not replace Radboud’s thesis; optional independent research remains outside the 24-course schedule.

Programming, mathematical methods and machine learning combine with robotics, reinforcement learning, signal processing and cognitive neuroscience. Human perception, higher cognition and language supply the cognitive-science strand of this broad AI programme.

Programming, algorithms, software, data infrastructure and mathematical modelling organise this computational AI programme. Machine learning, reinforcement learning, robotics and computer vision develop intelligent systems, supported by research methods, AI ethics and an introduction to brain and behaviour.

Cognitive neuroscience, human language, psychology and philosophy organise this cognitive AI programme. Programming, machine learning, neural networks, computer vision, optimisation and statistics connect the study of mind and brain to computational methods; research training includes experimental design and evidence synthesis.
